examples_description: One small, real page per module: the recommended pattern, its source file and the guide that explains it. Development only.
examples_delete_body: They disappear until the example data is reset.
examples_loader_description: The loader awaits ensureQuery on the server; the component reads the same query with useSuspenseQuery, with no request while hydrating.
examples_loader_note: The server counts calls. Reloading adds one; hydrating adds none. Refetch to see it rise.
examples_streaming_description: The loader returns a promise without awaiting it: the page is sent at once and the slow part streams in when ready.
examples_streaming_note: Reload the page: the fallback appears first, then the value arrives in the same response.
examples_filters_description: The URL is the state: validated search params, a filter form that works without JavaScript, chips and pagination.
examples_filters_note: Every change updates the URL, so the result can be shared, reloaded and navigated with Back.
examples_masking_description: A dialog over a list whose URL is the item's own page: reload, a new tab or no JavaScript open the full page.
examples_masking_note: Look at the address bar after opening one, then press Back, or reload while it's open.
examples_masking_dialog_note: This dialog is the list with ?open=…; the address bar shows the task's own URL.
examples_masking_full_page: The task's own page, rendered on the server.
examples_forms_description: useAppForm with the field library and one Zod schema; server refusals land on the right field.
examples_forms_simple_note: Client validation only: errors appear after a field is left or on submit, with a summary at the top.
examples_forms_server_note: The server checks the same schema and its own rules. Try the username “taken”.
examples_forms_sent: Thanks, {name}. Nothing was sent: this is an example.
examples_forms_username_hint: “admin”, “root” and “taken” are refused by the server.
examples_table_description: The shared table with this feature's columns: sort links, selection with bulk actions, row menus and column visibility.
examples_table_note: Select rows for the bulk bar, sort by a header, hide columns from the Columns menu.
examples_optimistic_description: A TanStack DB collection: changes show at once and are rolled back if the server refuses them.
examples_optimistic_note: The server takes 0.6 s. With the switch on it refuses, and the tick goes back.
examples_preferences_description: Theme, sidebar and table settings in a TanStack Store backed by cookies, so the server renders them.
examples_preferences_note: Reload after a change: the page arrives already in that state, with no flash.
examples_permissions_description: The server checks every call; the UI only hides what the server would refuse.
examples_extras_description: Recipes for lists: CSV export, delete with undo, and saved views.
examples_extras_table_note: The toolbar exports the rows on screen as CSV and keeps named views (search strings) in this browser. Deleting hides the row at once; the request goes out when the toast closes without Undo.
examples_caching_description: Cache-Control for the CDN: s-maxage with stale-while-revalidate.
examples_caching_note: Only for pages that look the same to everyone. Check reads this page's own response header.
examples_jobs_description: A job as named steps, each retried with backoff; a finished step never runs again.
examples_jobs_note: The second step fails the chosen number of times. Three retries: four failures give up.
examples_jobs_gave_up: Gave up after the last retry.
examples_contact_description: Honeypot, Turnstile when configured, and a database-backed rate limit.
examples_contact_note: Three messages per ten minutes per IP; the fourth is refused. Messages are logged, not emailed.
examples_permissions_you_note: From the session loaded with the page. Sign in as different users to compare.
examples_permissions_hidden: <Can permission="test-crud:read"> shows its fallback: you lack the permission.
examples_permissions_server_note: Both buttons always call the server, whatever the UI thinks.
examples_attachments_description: Images go straight from the browser to Cloudinary with a server signature, then the server verifies them.
examples_attachments_note: Submitting shows what a feature would save. Unsaved uploads are deleted by the daily cleanup.
examples_attachments_no_permission: Sign in as a user with the attachments:upload permission to try uploads.
examples_seo_description: seo() builds the title, description, canonical, hreflang, Open Graph, Twitter tags and JSON-LD.
examples_seo_meta_note: Dev pages are noindex; public pages use the same call without it.
examples_i18n_description: Paraglide messages called at render time, and the app's Intl helpers for numbers, money, dates and sizes.
examples_i18n_messages_note: Switch the language in the header: the server renders this page in it.
examples_i18n_formats_note: Nepali uses Devanagari digits; dates are in Asia/Kathmandu time.
examples_idempotency_description: A double submit or a retry after a lost response runs the action once: the server answers repeats of a key with the first result.
examples_idempotency_demo: Send the same message twice at once
examples_idempotency_note: Each button sends two requests together, like a double click. With a key, the second gets the first one's result instead of sending again.
examples_idempotency_outcome: Sent: {sent}. Answered with the first result: {replayed}.
examples_errors_description: Loader errors render the localized error or 404 page with the right status; action errors become toasts.
examples_errors_page_note: Each link reloads this page with an error. Use Back to return.
examples_errors_action_note: The page stays; the refusal is shown as a toast.
examples_analytics_description: Nothing is tracked before consent; flags are evaluated on the server and rendered with the page.
examples_analytics_consent_note: Changing it here is the same as using the banner.
examples_analytics_dropped: Not sent: analytics isn't running (no consent or not configured).
examples_analytics_flags_note: Evaluated on the server in the loader; unknown flags are off.
portfolio_footer_colophon_body: Set in Eczar, one display face for both scripts, with Inter and Noto Sans Devanagari for reading. Every mountain is drawn in code from its own seed; the sky follows the hour in Kathmandu. Built with TanStack Start, rendered on the server, in English and Nepali.
portfolio_process_intro: Five stages, usually eight to sixteen weeks. You see working software every week, and nothing ships without a number that says it worked.
portfolio_voices_heading: Kind words from people I’ve built with
portfolio_work_description: Case studies in fintech, commerce, realtime collaboration, developer tools and civic tech, from the first schema to launch day.
portfolio_about_description: The developer behind the work: ten years of full-stack product engineering from Kathmandu, the principles behind it and the teams along the way.
portfolio_journal_description: Essays on building for the web: server rendering, two scripts on one page, slow networks and boring databases.
portfolio_contact_description: Start a project or just say hello. One email address, a reply within two working days, from Kathmandu.
portfolio_contact_intro: Tell me about the problem, not the solution: who it’s for, what’s in the way, and how you’ll know it worked.
portfolio_contact_fit_1: You want a partner who ships, not a vendor who quotes.
portfolio_contact_fit_2: Your users include people on slow phones and slower networks.
portfolio_contact_fit_3: You’d rather launch something small and real than plan something big.
portfolio_not_found_title: This page wandered off the trail.
portfolio_not_found_body: The project or article you’re looking for doesn’t exist, or it moved. The rest of the story is still here.

examples_components_description: The admin kit on one page: stat cards and charts, data display, dialogs, hooks and the Graphite primitives.
examples_fields_description: Localized text, slugs, sortable lists, content blocks, key-value pairs and relations, in one form.
kit_stats_note: StatCard with a sparkline; AreaChart, BarChart and DonutChart load Recharts on demand into a box of fixed size, so nothing shifts.
kit_display_note: DetailLayout with an aside, DescriptionList, a status map, RelativeTime, CopyButton, ActivityFeed, UserCell with a hover card, and both kinds of EmptyState.
kit_dialogs_note: useConfirm() asks and returns a promise; FormDialog and FormSheet hold a form with its error summary, Save and Cancel, and ask before throwing edits away. The sheet also opens with the shortcut.
kit_confirm_body: Nothing is deleted in this example; the toast says what you chose.
kit_form_description: Type a name and save; close it after typing to see the discard question.
kit_hooks_note: useDebouncedValue waits until typing stops; useMediaQuery answers after hydration (the server says no).
kit_primitives_note: The shadcn primitives restyled for Graphite: alerts in the status tones, tabs, progress, spinner, button group, toggle, scroll area and accordion.
kit_alert_body: Alerts use the status colours, tested at 4.5:1 in every theme and accent.
kit_faq_what_body: The shared components every admin page and app is built from, so features only supply data, columns, fields and actions.
kit_faq_where_body: In docs/guides/design-system.md, under Components, with a story for each in Storybook.

kit_fields_relations_note: Search the example tasks on the server as you type.

apps_description: Small, complete apps you can try right now, without signing up. What you make in them is yours alone.
apps_guest_note: No sign-up needed: you get a guest session with sample data, deleted after {days} days. Create an account at any time to keep what you made.
kanban_tagline: Boards, columns and cards you move with a mouse or the keyboard.
kanban_description: Plan work on boards of columns and cards. Drag a card to move it, or use the keyboard; give cards labels, due dates and checklists.
kanban_seo_description: A Kanban board to try in your browser: move cards by dragging or with the keyboard, with labels, due dates and checklists. No sign-up needed.
kanban_feature_move: Move with a mouse or the keyboard
kanban_feature_move_body: Drag cards and columns, or focus a handle: Alt with the arrow keys moves a card up, down or into the next column.
kanban_feature_details_body: Every card can carry coloured labels, a due date that turns red once it passes, and a checklist.
kanban_feature_private_body: Your boards are yours alone: nobody else can see or change them.
kanban_empty_body: Create a board to start planning.
kanban_board_hint: Drag cards between columns, or focus a card's handle and press Alt with the arrow keys.
kanban_delete_board_body: Its columns and cards are deleted with it. This can't be undone.
kanban_delete_column_body: The cards in it ({count}) are deleted with it. This can't be undone.
kanban_drag_instructions: To move it, press Space, then the arrow keys, then Space again to drop it, or Escape to cancel. Alt with an arrow key moves it at once.
kanban_rolled_back: That change didn't save, so it was undone.
kanban_quota_boards: You have {max} boards, the most allowed. Delete one to make another.
kanban_quota_cards: You have {max} cards, the most allowed. Delete some to add more.
kanban_quota_columns: A board can have {max} columns at most.
kanban_seed_drag_body: Grab the handle on the left and drop the card in another column. Or focus the handle, press Space, use the arrow keys and press Space again.
kanban_seed_keyboard: Try Alt with the arrow keys
kanban_seed_keyboard_body: With this card's handle focused, Alt with up or down moves it in its column; Alt with left or right moves it to the next column.
kanban_seed_add: Add a card of your own
kanban_seed_explore: Open a card to edit it
kanban_seed_started_body: Done: you're here. Create an account to keep this board.
notes_tagline: Rich-text notes with tags, images and full-text search, in English or Nepali.
notes_description: Write notes with headings, lists and links, add tags and pictures, pin what matters and find anything with full-text search, in English or Nepali. Share a read-only copy when you want to.
notes_seo_description: A notes app to try in your browser: rich text, tags, images, pinning and full-text search that works in English and Nepali. No sign-up needed.
notes_feature_search_body: Full-text search over titles and text, in English and Nepali, with phrases in quotes and words to leave out.
notes_feature_write_body: Headings, lists, quotes, code and links, with tags and up to eight pictures per note.
notes_feature_share_body: A private link to a read-only copy, which you can turn off at any time. Notes are private otherwise.
notes_no_matches_body: Try other words, or clear the search or the tag.
notes_empty_body: Write your first note: a list, an idea, something to remember.
notes_rolled_back: That change couldn't be saved, so it was undone.
notes_delete_body: The note and its pictures are deleted for good. A shared link to it stops working.
notes_editor_description: Changes are saved when you press Save.
notes_field_tags_hint: Up to {max} tags of at most {length} characters. Press Enter after each.
notes_share_description: Anyone with the link can read this note, but not change it. Search engines never list it.
notes_unshare_body: The link stops working at once. Sharing again makes a new link.
notes_share_guest: Guests can't share notes: a shared note is public, so it needs an account.
notes_toast_shared: The note is shared. Copy the link to send it.
notes_toast_unshared: The note is no longer shared.
notes_shared_footer: Shared from Notes, a small app on this site.
notes_quota: You have reached the limit of {max} notes. Delete some to write more.
notes_seed_welcome_body: This is a note. Open it to edit the text, the tags and the pictures, then press Save.
notes_seed_welcome_format: Use the toolbar for headings, lists, quotes and links.
notes_seed_welcome_tags: Tags group notes: pick one above the list to see only its notes.
notes_seed_search_body: Type words in the search box to find notes that contain them, in the title or the text. Put a phrase in quotes to match it exactly, and a minus before a word to leave it out.
notes_seed_ideas_one: A morning walk up to Swayambhu.
notes_seed_ideas_two: Momos at the new place in Jhamsikhel.
links_tagline: Short links with QR codes and click statistics.
links_description: Turn long addresses into short links, print them as QR codes and see how many people follow them, from where and on what device. Pause a link or give it an end date whenever you like.
links_seo_description: A link shortener to try in your browser: short links, QR codes as SVG or PNG, and clicks by day, referrer, country and device. No sign-up needed.
links_feature_stats_body: Clicks per day for a month, the sites they came from, countries and devices.
links_feature_qr_body: Every link has a QR code to download as SVG for print or PNG for screens.
links_feature_private_body: No IP addresses are stored: only the referring site, a country and the kind of device.
links_new_description: Paste a long address. Leave the short name empty for a random one.
links_field_slug_hint: 3 to 32 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens. It can't be changed later.
links_field_expires_hint: The last day it works (Nepal time). Leave empty to keep it working.
links_guest_note: Your links start working when you have an account: guests can try everything, but their links don't redirect anyone.
links_empty_body: Make your first short link: paste any long address.
links_toast_paused: Paused: the link doesn't redirect anyone now.
links_delete_body: The link stops working and its statistics are deleted. Its short name becomes free, so someone else could take it; to keep it, pause the link instead.
links_days_label: Clicks per day over the last 30 days
links_error_slug: Use 3 to 32 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens.
links_error_slug_reserved: That name is reserved. Choose another.
links_error_slug_taken: That short name is taken. Choose another.
links_error_target_url: Enter a full web address starting with http:// or https://.
links_error_target_long: Addresses can have at most {max} characters.
links_error_target_self: A short link can't point to this site.
links_error_expiry_past: The last day can't be in the past.
links_quota: You have reached the limit of {max} links. Delete some to make more.
links_moderation_description: Every short link people made in the Links app. Block one that misleads or harms; its owner can't turn it back on.
links_moderation_search: Short name, address, title or owner
links_moderation_empty: Nobody has made a short link yet.
links_moderation_empty_filtered: No short link matches these filters.
links_block_body: The link stops redirecting at once and its owner can't turn it back on. You can unblock it later.
expenses_tagline: Track spending, set budgets and import a bank's CSV.
expenses_description: Write down what you spend in rupees or dollars, see where it goes by category and month, and keep each category under a monthly budget. Bring in a bank statement as CSV, or take everything out the same way.
expenses_seo_description: An expense tracker to try in your browser: spending by category and month, monthly budgets, and CSV import and export, in rupees or dollars. No sign-up needed.
expenses_feature_charts_body: Spending by category and the last six months at a glance, in Nepali digits when you read in Nepali.
expenses_feature_budgets_body: Give a category a budget for the month and watch how much is left, or by how much you went over.
expenses_feature_csv_body: Import up to a thousand rows from your bank: choose the columns, check every row first, import once.
expenses_trend_label: Spending per month over six months, in {currency}
expenses_budget_remove_body: Only this month's budget goes; the expenses stay.
expenses_no_budgets: No budgets for {month} in {currency}. Give a category one to see what is left.
expenses_empty_body: Add what you spend as you go, or import a CSV from your bank.
expenses_delete_body: The expense is deleted for good.
expenses_error_amount_positive: Enter an amount greater than zero.
expenses_error_category_long: A category name has at most {max} characters.
expenses_error_category_taken: You already have a category with this name.
expenses_quota: You can keep up to {max} expenses.
expenses_categories_quota: You can have up to {max} categories.
expenses_categories_empty_body: Categories group your expenses and carry budgets. An import makes the ones it needs.
expenses_category_delete_body: Its expenses ({count}) stay, uncategorized; its budgets are removed.
expenses_import_description: A CSV file from your bank or a spreadsheet, up to 1,000 rows. Nothing is saved until you import.
expenses_import_file_hint: Up to 1 MB. Commas between columns, one expense per line.
expenses_import_error_parse: A quote opened on line {line} is never closed.
expenses_import_error_size: The file is larger than 1 MB.
expenses_import_error_empty: The file has no rows to import.
expenses_import_error_rows: An import takes at most {max} rows. Split the file.
expenses_import_header: The first row names the columns
expenses_import_map_required: Choose the date and amount columns to see the rows.
expenses_import_skipping: Rows with problems are left out: {count}
habits_tagline: Daily check-ins, streaks and a year at a glance.
habits_description: Pick the habits you want to keep and the days they are for, tick them off each day, and watch your streaks grow. A year of check-ins fits in one picture.
habits_seo_description: A habit tracker to try in your browser: check-ins in one tap, streaks and completion rates in Nepal time, and a year-long heatmap. No sign-up needed.
habits_feature_checkin_body: Tick a habit off for today or the days before; a habit can need several check-ins, like eight glasses of water.
habits_feature_streaks_body: Days a habit isn't meant for never break a streak, and today stays open until midnight in Kathmandu.
habits_feature_year_body: Every day of the last year in one heatmap, drawn on the server.
habits_empty_body: Start with one small thing you want to do most days.
habits_archive_empty_body: Archive a habit you have stopped; its history stays.
habits_archived_note: This habit is archived: it isn't in your daily list.
habits_delete_body: The habit and all its check-ins are deleted for good.
habits_field_target_hint: How many count as done, from 1 to {max}.
habits_error_day: Check-ins can be changed for today and the year before.
habits_quota: You can have up to {max} habits.
habits_heatmap_label: {name}: check-ins over the last year, done on {done} days
forms_tagline: Build a survey, share a link, see the answers.
forms_description: Put a survey together from nine kinds of question, preview it as people will see it, and publish it at a link of its own. Every answer lands in charts and a table you can export.
forms_seo_description: A survey builder to try in your browser: drag questions into a form, publish it at a short link, and read the answers as charts, a table or a CSV file. No sign-up needed.
forms_feature_build_body: Drag a kind of question into the form or add it with the keyboard, then set its wording, options and rules beside it.
forms_feature_share_body: A published form has a short link anyone can open and fill in, without an account. Take it down at any time.
forms_feature_results_body: Bars for every choice, the average of every rating, the newest written answers, and all responses as a CSV file.
forms_empty_body: Start a form, add a few questions and publish it to collect answers.
forms_quota: You can have up to {max} forms.
forms_delete_body: The form and its {count} responses are deleted for good.
forms_toast_published: Form published: anyone with the link can fill it in.
forms_toast_unpublished: Form taken down: its link no longer opens it.
forms_toast_problems: Some settings need fixing before the form can be saved.
forms_publish_guest: Guests can build and preview forms, but only an account can publish one.
forms_publish_empty: Add a question before publishing the form.
forms_live_body: Anyone with the link can fill it in. Saving changes what they see from then on.
forms_preview_note: A preview with your unsaved changes. Nothing you send here is stored.
forms_preview_empty: Add a question to see the form.
forms_preview_checked: Every answer passes. Nothing was sent.
forms_fields_full: A form can have up to {max} questions.
forms_drop_first: Drag a kind of question here, or choose one on the left.
forms_drop_here: Drop here to add it at the end.
forms_remove_body: The answers already given to it stay stored, but they leave the results. Nothing changes until you save.
forms_settings_hint: Select a question to change its settings.
forms_field_description_hint: Shown under the title: what the form is for and how the answers are used.
forms_field_max_choices_hint: Leave empty to allow any number.
forms_error_range: The largest value can't be below the smallest.
forms_error_max_choices_options: There are fewer options than that.
forms_error_option: Choose one of the options given.
forms_type_short_text_hint: A name, a word, a line
forms_type_consent_hint: A box to tick to agree
forms_default_consent: I agree to my answers being stored.
forms_public_footer: Made with Forms, a survey builder you can try for free.
forms_responses_full: This form isn't taking more responses.
forms_error_changed: This form changed while you were filling it in. Reload the page to see its questions now.
forms_results_description: Every response so far, by question and one by one.
forms_results_completion_hint: Of every question in every response
forms_results_empty_body: Publish the form and share its link: answers show up here as they come in.
forms_seed_description: Tell us about your visit: it takes a minute.
forms_seed_heard: How did you hear about us?
forms_seed_email: Your email, if you'd like a reply
forms_seed_comment_1: More seats by the window, please.
forms_seed_comment_2: The momo were great, the tea came a little late.
apps_usage_description: How the showcase apps are used: counts only, never what people wrote.
apps_usage_guests_hint: Each is deleted a week after it started.
apps_usage_people_label: Accounts and guests with data in each app
